company: Karuna Therapeutics, Inc., a Bristol Myers Squibb Co.
regs_in_letter: FD&C Act (no CFR section cited in letter text)
note: Text read via Exa fetch of fda.gov PDF (WebFetch returned raw PDF bytes).

cases.claim: “Cobenfy showed overall improvement across a range of schizophrenia symptoms . . .” | on-screen “improvement ACROSS A RANGE OF SYMPTOMS” with overlapping circles “POSITIVE SYMPTOMS” and “NEGATIVE SYMPTOMS”
cases.context: Opening on-screen symptom words include “Lack of emotion”, “Low motivation”, “Less social interaction”. Primary endpoint was PANSS total at Week 5; trials enrolled acute exacerbation patients, not designed to assess negative symptoms. SUPER does not mitigate.
cases.rationale: Implies improvement in both positive and negative symptoms when trials did not evaluate these as distinct groups.
cases.check: Do claims or visuals attribute efficacy to symptom subdomains (e.g., negative symptoms) not separately established by the pivotal endpoints?

cases.claim: “If you still have symptoms, be bold and ask your healthcare provider about Cobenfy . . . .”
cases.context: Placebo-controlled trials without active comparator; no treatment-refractory population enrolled.
cases.rationale: Suggests efficacy where other antipsychotics have failed, which has not been demonstrated.
cases.check: Does the piece imply use after failure of other therapies ('still have symptoms', 'when others haven't worked') without supporting data?

cases.claim: “Cobenfy is not an antipsychotic” with on-screen “not an antipsychotic”
cases.context: SUPER: “A muscarinic agonist (xanomeline) and a muscarinic antagonist (trospium chloride)”.
cases.rationale: Cobenfy is considered an antipsychotic based on its indication and effects, not mechanism.
cases.check: Rule: flag 'not a/an <drug class>' statements for verification against the product's therapeutic class.

cases.claim: Compelling, attention-grabbing visuals (frequent camera angle changes showing Bryan skateboarding, greeting a friend, petting a dog, and setting up his DJ booth) during the major statement.
cases.rationale: Visuals interfere with comprehension of the major statement.
cases.check: During the major statement, are visuals active/attention-grabbing (scene cuts, activities) such that they compete with risk comprehension?
